messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging Maria (on-call) — high streaming tail latency detected for hosted-inference in eu-west region. p95 spike to 320ms, p99 to 1.9s, and multiple streaming stalls reported. Alert group: STREAM_TAIL_LATENCY. Root cause unknown.

Maria: I’m on it. grabbing graphs now. please @Raj and @Olivia for networking + routing context.

Raj: looking — we’re seeing inter-AZ packet loss and a rise in retransmits on the egress NAT path for eu-west2. initial hypothesis: asymmetric routing after a route flap.

Olivia: confirmed SLO breach on customer-facing streaming endpoints, releasing paging to pager duty. Any correlation with deploys?

Maria: no recent code deploys to serving in the last hour. logs show many stalled websocket frames in the gateway.

Ben: customers reporting degraded experience (typing lags, partial responses). raising to P1 if persists.

Nora: grabbing host-level metrics. conntrack table usage trending up on nat-gw-03. ephemeral ports close to exhaustion for some source ranges.

Sam: I’m seeing spikes in DNS latency towards internal resolvers around the same time window. Could be both DNS + path causing backoffs.

Raj: attaching a small capture (trimmed) — tcpdump shows SYNs retransmitted, then packets taking a different AZ path with ~40ms extra RTT.

Maria: quick mitigation options?

Raj: 1) temporarily shift routing away from nat-gw-03 via route table change (fast). 2) scale NAT gateway pool to add capacity (slower). 3) enable fallback routing to eu-west1 for non-latency-sensitive traffic.

Olivia: Also can we reduce streaming buffer size/enable more aggressive keepalive to reduce stall surface while we fix network?

Maria: do option 1 first. Raj — can you announce the route detour? include BGP community to prefer local AZ.

Raj: executing now: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c3d --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0df12345
# replaced with nat-0ef67890 (eu-west2-b fallback)
```

Raj: route change pushed. propagating. watching metrics.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: route-change job completed by Raj at 3337001260.

Nora: conntrack freed up after detour, ephemeral ports usage dropping.

Sam: DNS p99 still elevated but less severe. Could be cached negative entries from the path; flushing internal resolver cache for eu-west2 now.

Maria: p95 down to 140ms, p99 trending to 520ms. streaming stall counts reduced by ~60%. good progress.

Ben: Customer ops note — active incidents page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3337001234. Added initial customer impact summary.

Olivia: pushing a temporary config: lower socket RTO on gateway to 50ms for streaming sockets to reduce tail holdouts. Patch applied.

Raj: we still see some sporadic retransmit bursts tied to one AZ ToR switch. networking team has opened a ticket with cloud provider; they’re investigating a fabric microburst affecting certain VPC paths.

Maria: OK. mitigation plan: - keep detour routing for 30m - scale NAT pool by +2 instances - keep socket RTO change - continue DNS cache flushes - if fabric ticket not resolved, fail traffic to eu-west1 fallback for heavy streaming.

Nora: scaling NAT gateway pool: triggering autoscale runbook now.

incident-bot: Autoscale action started at 3337001295 by Nora.

Nora: +2 nat gateways up, health checks green.

Maria: p99 now at 310ms. streaming stall metric essentially back to baseline.

Sam: cloud provider confirmed a partial fabric congestion in eu-west2-b; they’re rerouting affected spine links. estimated time to fix 45-60 min.

Ben: posted update to customers: initial mitigation in place, routing detour applied, scaling done. requesting customer impact classification to remain P1 until p99 < 300ms for 15m.

Olivia: agree. continuing to monitor. setting a dashboard alert to notify if p99 creeps above 400ms.

Maria: handing off to Raj (next on-call network) for continued monitoring & provider follow-up. I’ll start the incident writeup and timeline.

Raj: ACK — I’ll keep a watch and follow provider updates. If fabric repair delayed beyond ETA, will execute cross-region failover test to eu-west1 for streaming traffic.

incident-bot: On-call handoff: Maria -> Raj at 3337001340.

Maria: quick notes for postmortem: interestingly we saw conntrack pressure on nat-gw-03 concurrent with path shift; likely amplified by DNS timeouts causing retries. Action items: 1) add conntrack headroom to NAT AMI, 2) improve DNS resolver redundancy across AZs, 3) add route-change playbook to prefer AZ-local NATs proactively, 4) sharpen streaming socket keepalive defaults.

Raj: added: verify BGP pathology with provider, request ToR-level counters for that timeframe.

Ben: I’ll coordinate customer comms once we have provider confirmation and final impact window.

Maria: thanks team. closing active mitigation. will reopen if metrics regress. :white_check_mark:

Raj: metrics look stable for now. leaving monitoring hooks on.

incident-bot: Incident status updated to "mitigated (monitoring)" at 3337001350.
